title: Sliding Window Maximum
contract: Return the maximum in each length-k window, where 1 ≤ k ≤ n.
brute: int[] out=new int[a.length-k+1];for(int l=0;l<out.length;l++){int max=Integer.MIN_VALUE;for(int i=l;i<l+k;i++)max=Math.max(max,a[i]);out[l]=max;emit("Scan one complete window","range",new int[]{l,l+k-1},"output",out);}return out;
optimal: int[] out=new int[a.length-k+1];Deque<Integer> q=new ArrayDeque<>();for(int i=0;i<a.length;i++){while(!q.isEmpty()&&q.peekFirst()<=i-k)q.removeFirst();while(!q.isEmpty()&&a[q.peekLast()]<=a[i])q.removeLast();q.addLast(i);if(i>=k-1)out[i-k+1]=a[q.peekFirst()];emit("Expire old indices and remove dominated candidates","index",i,"candidate indices",q,"output",out);}return out;
reasoning: Independent scans repeat almost all comparisons between adjacent windows.
Keep indices in decreasing value order; the front is the maximum and indices outside the window expire from the front.
A newer value at least as large dominates an older smaller value because it also expires later. Every index enters and leaves the deque once.
